title: Audiological and Postoperative Outcomes in Patients with Cochlear Implants at the Heidelberg University Department of Otolaryngology—a Retrospective Analysis of the Past 10 Years
summary:
In this study, we are reviewing patient data retrospectively. We want to determine how well treatment with a hearing implant (cochlear implant, or CI for short) has worked.
We are examining the following aspects:
• Hearing and speech ability: We compare hearing and speech comprehension before and after surgery using standardized hearing tests.
• Complications: We record all medical problems that occurred after surgery—such as inflammation or the need to replace the implant.
• Progress in recovery: Based on follow-up reports, we assess how the subsequent therapy (outpatient or in a clinic) proceeded, how speech developed, and how well the device was adjusted.
How we analyze the data:
We clearly summarize general patient data (such as age and gender) and test results. To identify differences before and after surgery, we use mathematical comparison tests. We also use statistical models to determine which factors most influence the success of the surgery and how frequently complications occur over time.
conditions: Presence of otological and audiological implants

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of all patients who underwent cochlear implantation between 2015 and 2025
